blocks.text: When sales slow down, the first thought is usually to spend more on advertising. In many of the businesses we see, the enquiries are already there. They arrive by phone, WhatsApp, email, and walk-ins. Some get a quick reply. Some wait days. Some are never answered at all.

dl.title: 30-day enquiry log
dl.desc: A one-page sheet to record every enquiry for 30 days, with a Friday review checklist.

blocks.text: Why it happens

dl.title: 30-day enquiry log
dl.desc: A one-page sheet to record every enquiry for 30 days, with a Friday review checklist.

items: Nobody owns the reply. Everyone assumes someone else has it.
Enquiries arrive in too many places: personal phones, shared inboxes, and social media messages.
Nothing is recorded, so nobody can see what was missed.
Busy days push enquiries to the bottom of the list, and they are forgotten.

dl.title: 30-day enquiry log
dl.desc: A one-page sheet to record every enquiry for 30 days, with a Friday review checklist.

blocks.text: None of these need new software to fix. They need an owner and a record.

blocks.text: The 30-day routine

dl.title: 30-day enquiry log
dl.desc: A one-page sheet to record every enquiry for 30 days, with a Friday review checklist.

blocks.text: For the next 30 days, do four things.

dl.title: 30-day enquiry log
dl.desc: A one-page sheet to record every enquiry for 30 days, with a Friday review checklist.

items.text: Name one person who owns every enquiry. They do not have to answer each one, but they make sure someone does.
Record every enquiry in one place. A notebook or a shared spreadsheet is enough. Write the date, how it arrived, what the person wanted, how long the reply took, and what happened.
Agree a reply time. Same day is a good start. Within an hour is better.
Review the record every Friday for 15 minutes. Look for enquiries with no outcome.

dl.title: 30-day enquiry log
dl.desc: A one-page sheet to record every enquiry for 30 days, with a Friday review checklist.

dl.title: 30-day enquiry log
dl.desc: A one-page sheet to record every enquiry for 30 days, with a Friday review checklist.

blocks.text: What to look for at the end

dl.title: 30-day enquiry log
dl.desc: A one-page sheet to record every enquiry for 30 days, with a Friday review checklist.

items: How many enquiries came in. Most owners are surprised.
How long replies took, on average and at worst.
Which channel brought the most enquiries, and which brought customers.
How many enquiries had no outcome. These are the sales you are losing.

dl.title: 30-day enquiry log
dl.desc: A one-page sheet to record every enquiry for 30 days, with a Friday review checklist.

blocks.text: Multiply the enquiries with no outcome by your average sale, and by how many in ten usually become customers. That gives a rough monthly cost of the gap. It is often enough to justify fixing it properly.
